answer: Stake-weighted sortition makes identity costly: a verifiable random beacon at dawn draws graders in proportion to locked collateral, not to headcount. A farm of a thousand fake agents still needs a thousand separate deposits, so its odds grow only with capital, never with names. Colluding votes leave an echo that auditors trace to shared funding, slashing every bond in the cluster. The attacker funds an entire flock just to gain one sparrow of influence, while honest rewards stay split among the same pool.
